'''Charles L. Kane''' ('''Charles Lewis Kane'''; born January 12, 1963) is a [[theoretical physics|theoretical]] [[condensed matter physics|condensed matter physicist]] and is the Christopher H. Browne Distinguished Professor of Physics at the [[University of Pennsylvania]]. He completed a B.S. in physics at the [[University of Chicago]] in 1985 and his Ph.D. at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1989. Prior to joining the faculty at the University of Pennsylvania he was a postdoctoral associate at [[IBM]]'s [[T. J. Watson Research Center]] working with his mentor [[Matthew P. A. Fisher]], among others.

Kane is notable for theoretically predicting the [[quantum spin Hall effect]] (originally in graphene) and what would later be known as [[topological insulator]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Brumfiel|first=Geoff|date=2010-07-01|title=Topological insulators: Star material|journal=Nature News|language=en|volume=466|issue=7304|pages=310–311|doi=10.1038/466310a|pmid=20631773|s2cid=11864273 |issn=1476-4687|doi-access=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hasan|first1=M. Zahid|last2=Kane|first2=Charles L.|date=2010-11-08|title=Topological Insulators|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/RevModPhys.82.3045|journal=Reviews of Modern Physics|language=en|volume=82|issue=4|pages=3045–3067|doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.82.3045|s2cid=16066223|issn=0034-6861|arxiv=1002.3895}}</ref>

He received the 2012 [[Dirac Medal (ICTP)|Dirac Prize]], along with [[Shoucheng Zhang]] and [[Duncan Haldane]], for their groundbreaking work on two- and three-dimensional [[topological insulators]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/prizes-awards/the-dirac-medal/the-medallists-%281%29/dirac-medallists-2012.aspx |title=Dirac prize citation - 2012 |access-date=2013-02-06 |archive-date=2015-06-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623025112/http://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/prizes-awards/the-dirac-medal/the-medallists-(1)/dirac-medallists-2012.aspx |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web
| last = Durrani, Matin
| title = Condensed-matter trio scoop Dirac prize - physicsworld.com
| access-date = 2013-02-06
| url = http://physicsworld.com/cws/article/news/2012/aug/08/condensed-matter-trio-scoop-dirac-prize
| date = 2012-08-08
}}</ref> In the same year he was also chosen for the inaugural class of Mathematics and the Physical Sciences [[Simons Investigator]]s.<ref>[https://simonsfoundation.org/program-areas/mathematics-and-physical-science/simons-investigators/ Simons Investigators]</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Penn’s Charles Kane Named Simons Investigator and Awarded $500,000 Grant |work=Penn News |url=http://www.upenn.edu/pennnews/news/penn-s-charles-kane-named-simons-investigator-and-awarded-500000-grant|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120730003744/http://www.upenn.edu/pennnews/news/penn-s-charles-kane-named-simons-investigator-and-awarded-500000-grant|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 30, 2012}}</ref> He also shared one of the 2013 [[Physics Frontiers prize]]s with [[Laurens W. Molenkamp]] and [[Shoucheng Zhang]] for their work on topological insulators.<ref>{{Cite web
| last = Hamish Johnston
| title = Higgs hunters and Stephen Hawking bag new $3m prizes - physicsworld.com
| access-date = 2013-02-06
| url = http://physicsworld.com/cws/article/news/2012/dec/11/higgs-hunters-and-stephen-hawking-bag-new-3m-prizes
| date = 2012-12-11
}}</ref> In 2018, he shared the [[BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Award|Frontiers of Knowledge Award]] with [[Eugene J. Mele]]. In 2019, was recognized with [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics]] with fellow University of Pennsylvania professor Eugene Mele.<ref>{{Cite web
| last = Baillie, Katherine Unger 
| title = Eugene Mele and Charles Kane to share Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics
| date = 17 October 2018
| access-date = 2018-10-17
| url = https://penntoday.upenn.edu/news/charles-kane-and-eugene-mele-share-breakthrough-prize-fundamental-physics
}}</ref> In 2025, he received the [[Lorentz Medal]], again for work on topological insulators.<ref>{{Cite web 
| title = Charles Kane Awarded 2026 Lorentz Medal
| date = 3 September 2025
| access-date = 2025-09-03
| url = https://pan-school.sas.upenn.edu/news/charles-kane-receive-2026-lorentz-medal#:~:text=Charles%20Kane%2C%20Christopher%20H.,groundbreaking%20contributions%20to%20theoretical%20physics.
}}</ref>
